## [0.25.0] - 2026-10-26

### Added

- **Help → Report a Problem…** (`help.reportProblem`, also a button in the Debug Log window) and **`editora
  --report`**: a problem report from the debug log (this session's and the one before), with the version, Java,
  OS and plugins. Paths in the home folder, the user name, e-mail addresses, credentials in URLs, authentication
  headers and token-shaped values are replaced first, and the report is shown, editable, before anything leaves
  the machine. **Open GitHub Issue** copies it and opens a new issue with it filled in (a report too long for the
  link is pasted from the clipboard instead); Copy and Save… are there for any other channel. `--report` writes
  the file to the current folder and opens the issue, for when Editora will not start. Nothing is sent by Editora
  itself: the user submits the issue. A new bug-report issue form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`) has
  the fields the link fills.
- **Run: Run Context at Caret** (`run.context`; Ctrl+Shift+F10 / ⌃⇧R in the IntelliJ keymaps, as IntelliJ's Run
  Context Configuration): runs the test at the caret (the whole test class above its declaration), else the class's
  `main` as its ▶ does, else the file; a Java class with neither says so. The chord used to rerun the last Maven goal.
- **Find Action knows other IDEs' names.** The command palette also finds commands by what IntelliJ IDEA and VS Code
  call them: Optimize Imports, Show Context Actions, Reformat Code, Find Usages, Parameter Info, Insert Live
  Template, Go to Test, Copy Reference, Show Call Hierarchy, Find Action, Super Method and others. The whole of
  such a name leads the titles it only fuzzily matches, so "go to test" finds Related File first. A command's own
  title, typed, comes before another command's other-IDE name.
- **Go to Super Method** (`lsp.gotoSuperMethod`; Ctrl+U / ⌘U in the IntelliJ keymaps, in Navigate and the editor's
  LSP submenu): from anywhere in a method (its `@Override` and Javadoc too, an anonymous class's method included,
  in a method, a field, an initializer or an enum constant), the method it overrides or implements: jdtls's answer,
  and the type hierarchy for what it misses, so an interface's default method and a method two interfaces declare
  go to each, and of two where one overrides the other, the nearer alone. A static or private method, or another
  overload, has none. In a lambda, its functional interface's method; in a constructor, the super constructor it
  calls, through `this(...)` too; on a type, its supertypes, the superclass first and each named by its type; a
  picker when there are several. It works the same in a library source tab, and says it is looking when a deep
  hierarchy takes a moment. A type parameter of any name (`Store<Item>`, `Handler<Req, Res>`) stands for the type
  it is given, and a method marked `@Override` is looked for up the hierarchy when jdtls finds nothing, as for an
  inner class of a generic class.
- **More IntelliJ and VS Code chords.** IntelliJ keymaps: Ctrl+I implements methods on Linux, Ctrl+Shift+= / - (⌘⇧= /
  ⌘⇧-, and the numpad's Ctrl+Shift++ / -) expand and collapse all folds, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C copies the qualified name,
  Ctrl+Alt+F7 finds usages, and menus name Alt+Enter for Code Actions. VS
  Code keymaps: Ctrl+F12 Go to Implementation, Alt+F12 Peek Definition,
  Ctrl+T Go to Symbol in Workspace.
- **Doctor names the Java jdtls runs on**, with its version, and warns when its launcher's `python3` is missing, when
  no Java new enough for the installed jdtls is found, and when the JDK the window's project gets (the release its
  build file states, `${…}` properties, Spring Boot's `java.version`, a Kotlin `jvmToolchain` and a reactor's
  modules read, else the default) has no sources (`arg0` parameters), naming each and the package that adds them.
- Navigate lists Go to Declaration, Peek Definition and Copy Qualified Name; the editor's LSP submenu lists Call and
  Type Hierarchy.
- **Code-action lightbulb in the gutter** (IntelliJ's intention bulb). When the caret rests on a line where the
  language server has a fix for an error, a red bulb with a `!` shows in the gutter; an amber one for other quick
  actions, a warning's included. Refactorings, source actions and Add Javadoc, which servers offer nearly
  everywhere, light nothing. Click it for the list Alt+Enter shows, for its own line; its tooltip names the chord.
  It goes as soon as the caret leaves the line or the line is edited, shows only in the focused view of a split and
  never asks for a tab that is not on screen (it keeps its bulb, and asks again when shown), takes its colours from
  the editor theme (accent and danger in themes without their own; the foreground colour in Summer Dark, Navy Dark,
  Fall Dark and Blacky, whose accent is the bookmark's yellow), and
  never shifts the text: it uses the bookmark column. Settings ▸ Code Completion ▸ Language server features, on by
  default.
- **Problem counter at the top right of the editor** (IntelliJ's inspection widget): the file's errors and warnings
  with their glyphs, or a green check when the server found none, and previous/next arrows that go through that
  file's problems. Click the counts to show or hide Problems. It says Analyzing… until the server has checked the
  file (for Java, until the project is loaded: jdtls's first, empty list is no check), again after a restart, and
  Not checked when its project did not import. Shown while a language server checks the file and the
  code pane is at least 520 px wide; a setting beside the lightbulb's turns it off.
  Settings schema 146→147, additive.
- **Doctor: Check for Newer Versions.** A button in Doctor's header asks npm, the Go module proxy, GitHub and
  HashiCorp for the latest release of each working language server or tool that Editora installs at its latest
  release (Pyright, typescript-language-server, the JSON/HTML/CSS, Bash, YAML, Dockerfile, TOML and Astro servers,
  gopls, clangd, lua-language-server, tinymist, terraform-ls and the Mermaid CLI). Ones with a newer release move to
  **Updates available** at the top, with **Update…**. Nothing is looked up until you click, and a Refresh keeps
  what the check found. Pinned servers are not looked up: a new Editora release brings their new versions.
- **Doctor: Update for a TypeScript server without tsserver.** The warning for a typescript-language-server with no
  TypeScript, or with TypeScript 7 (which has no tsserver), now has the **Update…** button its tip mentioned; it
  reinstalls the server with TypeScript 6. Update on a row of the Java, Python or JavaScript support now
  reinstalls only that row's tool.
- **Settings sync carries your shortcuts.** A new **Shortcuts** switch on Settings ▸ Sync (on by default) syncs
  the key bindings you changed, in every keymap and for both Windows/Linux and macOS, as `keybindings.json` in the
  sync repository. They merge chord by chord like snippets; which keymap each computer uses stays its own. A change
  syncs shortly after you rebind, reset or switch keymaps. Settings schema 145→146, additive.
- **Surround With** (`snippets.surround`, Code ▸ Surround With…; Ctrl+Alt+T / Cmd+Alt+T in the IntelliJ keymaps)
  lists only the snippets that wrap a selection and puts the selection inside the chosen one; with nothing
  selected it wraps the current line.
- **Java: Excluded types** (Settings ▸ Code Completion ▸ Language server features): the packages and types
  completion, auto-import, Go to Symbol and Search Everywhere leave out. The default is vscode-java's list,
  which includes `java.awt.*`. Settings schema 144→145, additive.
- **Go to Implementation lists library implementations.** When an implementation lives in the JDK or a dependency,
  every implementation is listed in a picker with its package, instead of one being opened with no word of the
  others.
- **Doctor: Update for servers and tools older than Editora's.** Editora installs jdtls, the JavaScript debugger,
  the Maven pom.xml server, Groovy's gls, Metals, the Kotlin server, clojure-lsp, ShellCheck and shfmt at the
  exact release it is tested with. When a new Editora moves to a newer release, Doctor now marks a copy installed
  under the old one with a warning that names both versions and an **Update…** button, which installs the new
  release and restarts the server on it. Each install now records its version (`.editora-install` in its folder);
  for copies from before this, Doctor reads the version from the files or from `--version` where it can, and
  offers Update where it cannot tell (a Kotlin server from an earlier Editora). Install also replaces Editora's
  own copy that is known to be older, as it already did for jdtls.
- **A Clojure debugging sample.** `samples/debug/clojure/` is the same shelf as a small standalone Clojure CLI
  project (four namespaces, a script, six green clojure.test tests) with a `break here` comment at every spot
  worth a breakpoint: a `loop/recur` whose bindings change on every pass, an anonymous fn, a recursion, three
  named worker threads, a caught and an uncaught exception, and a script's top-level forms. `clojure -M:run`
  and `clojure -M:test` run it outside Editora.
- **Complete Statement** (`edit.completeStatement`, Code ▸ Complete Statement; Ctrl+Shift+Enter / Cmd+Shift+Enter in
  the IntelliJ keymaps), as IntelliJ's Complete Current Statement: in Java, C, C++, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP
  and Kotlin it closes the line's open string and brackets, adds the `;` (not in Kotlin) or the `{ }` block a
  control header, type or method needs, and leaves the caret where the next code goes. A finished statement gets a
  new line below; other languages get Insert Line Below. Every caret, one undo step.
- **Java: Smart Type completion** (`lsp.smartTypeCompletion`, Edit menu; Ctrl+Shift+Space in the IntelliJ keymaps),
  as IntelliJ's: the completion list holds only what fits the type expected at the caret. The type comes from a
  declaration (`String s = `), an assignment, `return` (the method's return type), a condition (`if (`, `&&`) or
  a call's argument (signature help). Fields, variables and methods of a fitting type stay, `null` for an object
  and `true`/`false` for a boolean; after `new`, the classes that implement the type. Where the code states no
  type the full list opens, and the status bar says so.
- **One Java server per project, whichever windows it is open in.** A second window on a Java project joins the
  jdtls the first one runs instead of starting another, which imported the project again on a second
  workspace and used as much memory again (about 1.5 GB). Both windows see its diagnostics; a question the
  server asks goes to the window you are working in. Closing one window leaves the server to the other, and
  Restart Language Servers in either restarts it for both.
- **Java: organize imports and format on save.** Two settings under Settings ▸ Code Completion ▸ Language server features: after you
  save a Java file, jdtls organizes its imports and/or formats it, and the file is saved again when that changed
  it, as IntelliJ's Actions on Save do. Both are off by default; autosave never runs them, and an ambiguous import
  is left out rather than asked about. Settings schema 143→144, additive.
- **Java: clean-ups.** **Code ▸ Clean Up File** applies the jdtls clean-ups chosen under Settings ▸ Code
  Completion ▸ Language server features (add `@Override` and `@Deprecated`, drop redundant modifiers, qualify
  members, add `final`, pattern-matching `instanceof`, switch expressions, lambdas, try-with-resources, text
  blocks and more; 19 in all, four on by default). **Clean up on save (Java)** runs them after an explicit save,
  before organizing imports and formatting.
- **Java: Lombok on request.** A project whose build declares Lombok but has not downloaded it yet is offered
  Lombok 1.18.48 from Maven Central (checked by SHA-256 into `plugins/lsp/lombok`); its Java server then restarts
  with Lombok as its agent.
- **Java: a project's own code style reaches jdtls.** IntelliJ's import settings in `.editorconfig`
  (`ij_java_imports_layout`, `ij_java_class_count_to_use_import_on_demand`,
  `ij_java_names_count_to_use_import_on_demand`) become jdtls's import order and `*` thresholds, and the Eclipse
  formatter profile the build formats with (Spotless's `<eclipse><file>` or `eclipse().configFile(…)`, else an
  `eclipse-formatter.xml` at the root) is what Format Document uses.
- **Java: chain completion.** In an argument or assignment, completion also offers calls that produce the
  expected type, such as `Collectors.toList()` inside `collect(`.
- **Java: Extract Method, Variable and Field at the caret, Introduce Parameter, and a warning before a risky
  move.** Editora now declares jdtls's `inferSelectionSupport`: with nothing selected the extract actions are
  offered, and Editora asks the server which expressions are there and lets you pick one when there are several.
  Introduce Parameter is offered as its own refactoring. Extract to Field and Convert Local to Field ask where
  to initialize the field when there is a choice. A Move Instance Method that jdtls finds problems with (jdtls
  1.61 final and newer) now shows those problems and moves only if you continue; before, it was applied anyway.
- **Java: Go to Symbol in Workspace finds methods and JDK or library types.** jdtls was never asked for method
  symbols, and its matches inside JDK or dependency classes (`jdt://`) were dropped. They are listed after the
  project's own, labelled with their module or jar, and open as library source.
- **File structure in the Project Map.** A file row whose language the Structure tool window can outline
  (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Kotlin, Markdown headings, Typst, `.http` requests, Clojure, poms…)
  gets a Structure icon before its preview eye. It opens a column of the file's declarations, the way a
  folder's chevron opens its children; a declaration that holds others — a class's members, a heading's
  subsections — has a chevron of its own and opens a further column, and a file with one top-level type opens
  its members straight away. Clicking a declaration opens a floating preview card of only its lines: its block
  with the doc comment and annotations above it, numbered as the file numbers them (in the narrowed amber),
  coloured as in the editor, sized to fit, and titled "App.java › add()". Open goes to the declaration; Open
  Narrowed, in the card's and the row's menu, opens the file narrowed to the declaration's fold block, as the
  Structure window's Narrow to fold region does. Several declarations of one file can be open side by side
  under the usual eight-card limit. The columns and cards follow edits: an open file's unsaved text is what is
  outlined (with the language server's symbols when the Structure window has them), a closed file is read
  again when it changes on disk, and a card whose declaration was removed keeps its last lines and says so.
  The arrow along the flow opens a file's structure, Enter on a declaration opens its card, and the columns
  are part of Print and PDF output. Nothing about it is remembered across restarts.
- **About says whether Editora is up to date.** Under the version, the About panel now reads "You are up to date."
  or "Update available: X.Y.Z" (a link to that release), then when the last check answered and a **Check now**
  link that asks GitHub again and updates the panel in place, failures included. Before any check has answered it
  says so instead of claiming anything. The answer is kept in the preferences (`latestReleaseVersion`,
  `latestReleaseUrl`, `lastUpdateCheckOkEpoch`; settings schema 142→143, additive), so it survives a restart: the
  status-bar update notice now also comes back after a restart until the release is opened or installed, instead
  of waiting for the next day's check.
- **Java: Undo Last Refactoring.** A rename, move or other refactoring that changed several files can be undone in
  all of them at once: Undo in one of its files asks whether to undo it everywhere, and **LSP: Undo Last
  Refactoring** does it from the palette. Renamed files move back and created ones are removed. Before, Undo
  reverted one file and left the rest of the project renamed.
- **Java: renaming a `.java` file or a package folder in the Project tree renames the class or package.** The
  tree asks jdtls (`workspace/willRenameFiles`) for the edits first, so references, `package` lines and imports
  follow; before, the class kept its old name and the project stopped compiling.
- **Java: Generate, Refactor This and a command per refactoring.** **LSP: Generate…** lists the generators
  (getters/setters, constructors, toString, equals/hashCode, overrides, delegates), **LSP: Refactor This…** the
  refactorings at the caret, and Extract Variable / Constant / Field / Method, Introduce Parameter, Inline, Move,
  Change Signature and Override/Implement Methods each have a command that runs the one jdtls offers there. They
  are in a new **Code ▸ Refactor** submenu; before, all of them were reachable only through the quick-fix list.
- **Next / Previous Problem and Show Problem at Caret.** Jump between the file's errors (warnings when there
  are none) and read the one under the caret without the mouse.
- **The "IntelliJ IDEA" keymap uses IntelliJ's Java chords:** Alt+Enter for quick fixes, Shift+F6 Rename,
  F2/Shift+F2 next/previous problem, Ctrl+F1 problem at caret, Alt+Insert Generate, Ctrl+Alt+L/O format and
  organize imports, Ctrl+N / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N symbols, Ctrl+Alt+B implementations, Ctrl+Shift+B type,
  Ctrl+H / Ctrl+Alt+H hierarchies, Ctrl+P parameter info, Ctrl+Alt+V/C/F/M/P/N, F6 Move, Ctrl+F6 Change
  Signature, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T Refactor This, Ctrl+O Override, Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right Back/Forward (and the macOS
  equivalents). F2 is no longer Rename and Alt+Insert no longer New File (now Ctrl+Alt+Insert) in that keymap.
  The default Emacs keymap gains a `C-c l` prefix for the language-server commands, `M-g M-n`/`M-g M-p` for
  problems and `M-,`/`C-M-,` for back/forward; every keymap now binds Back and Forward.
- **LSP: Clean Java Workspace and Restart.** Stops the project's Java server, deletes its index and the classpath
  and source folders it worked out, and imports the project afresh — the cure for a stale or corrupt jdtls
  workspace, which Restart Language Servers kept and Clear Java Index Caches skipped while in use.
- **Java: navigation inside library source.** In a JDK or dependency tab opened by Go to Definition, hover, Find
  References, Go to Implementation / Type Definition / Declaration and the call and type hierarchies now work, asked
  of the server that opened it; before, only Go to Definition did and the rest said "No language server for this
  file". JDK and library nodes in the hierarchies open as library source too.
- **Java: `/**` gives the declaration's Javadoc.** Typing `/**` above a method or class closes the comment and offers
  jdtls's "Javadoc comment" template, with `@param`, `@return` and `@throws` for that declaration. Enter instead
  still splits the comment as before.
- **Java: rename what an extraction created.** After Extract Method, Variable, Constant or Field the caret is on the
  name jdtls picked (`d`, `getTotal`) and Rename opens on it.
- **Java: Search Everywhere finds JDK and library classes.** With a Java server running, `List`, `Assertions` and
  the other classes the project's index cannot see are listed under Symbols after the project's own, and open as
  library source.
- **Format Document formats only the selection when there is one** (`textDocument/rangeFormatting`), whole lines,
  as IntelliJ's Reformat Code does; before, the whole file was reformatted under a selection.
- **Change Signature and Move show their files before applying.** When they change other files, the rename preview
  lists them, ticked, and an unticked file is left alone; before, both applied unseen.
- **Related File (test ⇄ subject) is in the Navigate menu**, and on `C-c S-t` (`C-c T`) in the Emacs keymap.
- **Java: Lombok.** jdtls runs with Lombok as its Java agent for a project whose build declares Lombok (Maven
  `org.projectlombok`, Gradle's Freefair plugin), using the newest Lombok jar already in the local Maven or Gradle
  cache, as vscode-java does with its own. Before, every getter of an `@Data` or `@Getter` class was an error.
  Nothing is downloaded: a project built for the first time gets it when its server next starts.
- **Java: null analysis from the project's annotations.** With JSpecify, `javax.annotation`, Spring or Eclipse
  null annotations on the classpath, jdtls checks `@Nullable` and `@NonNull` use, as IntelliJ's inspections do.
- **Java: static members of JUnit and Mockito are completed without an import** (`assertEquals`, `mock`,
  `when`…), and the static import is added.
- **Surround With.** Insert Snippet over selected lines wraps them in the Java `if`, `for`, `while`, `do`, `try`
  and `synchronized` snippets, re-indented; Ctrl+Alt+T (Cmd+Alt+T on macOS) in the IntelliJ keymap. A snippet's
  multi-line variable now keeps the indentation of the line it is on.
- **Java: Move into a new package.** Move's package list ends with "New package…": type the name and the folder
  is created under the current source root and the file moved there.
- **Java: Related File offers to create a missing test.** On a class under `src/main/java` with no test, it offers
  a JUnit 5 test in the same package under `src/test/java`, and opens it.

### Changed

- **IntelliJ keymap: Ctrl+J / ⌘J is Insert Snippet** (IntelliJ's Insert Live Template), which lost its only chord
  when Ctrl+Alt+T became Surround With.
- **Menus drop the palette's category prefixes** ("Edit:", "Go:", "Snippet:") where the rest still says what the
  row does, as they already dropped "LSP:".
- **Completion matches camel humps first:** `vO` puts `valueOf` first and `st` finds `toString`; two typed
  letters no longer match letters scattered through a name.
- **IntelliJ keymap (macOS): ⌘N is Generate in the editor**, as in IntelliJ, and New in the Project tree; New File
  moves to ⌃⌘N. ⌃I is Override/Implement Methods, and ⌘[ / ⌘] go back and forward. On Linux and Windows,
  Alt+Insert is New in the Project tree too.
- **Generate (Alt+Insert) lists only generators**, and Override/Implement Methods sits next to it in the Code menu;
  jdtls's generator quick assists no longer crowd Alt+Enter, and Inline (Ctrl+Alt+N) no longer offers Make
  Static.
- **Menu rows drop the palette's "LSP:" prefix**, and the editor's LSP submenu gains Peek Definition, Refactor
  This… and Generate….
- **Go to Symbol and Search Everywhere rank the exact class first** and a library class nested in another last,
  and leave out the excluded types (no more `sun.*` or `Arrays.ArrayList` above `java.util.ArrayList`).
- **The Default JDK's hint says what it drives** (Gradle imports and the Java server's default JDK too), and
  changing it while jdtls runs says to restart the language servers.
- **Plurals:** "1 file", "1 change", "1 reference", "1 item" in the References, Problems, hierarchy, rename
  preview and refactoring-undo counts, in all six languages.
- **Project Map preview and note cards move and zoom with the map.** Panning carries a card along with the
  columns under it, zooming scales it with them (the card's − / + still sizes its text on top), and a card can
  be dragged past the edge of the visible canvas the way a column can, instead of stopping at the panel's edge. Its resize grip now allows up to the panel's
  size wherever the card stands, and resizing the panel no longer pushes cards back inside it. Whatever part of a
  card lies outside the map is clipped, so a card never paints over the Map's filter bar or breadcrumbs.
- **Refactor: the preview's right-click menu owns its own state and moved to `editor.markdown`.** `PreviewMenu` is now an object the buffer holds: the seven export and print actions the window injects, and what the pointer was on when the menu opened, live in it instead of in eleven `EditorBuffer` fields read from outside. The window injects the actions through `buffer.previewMenu()` (`setExportPdf`, `setPrint`, …) in place of seven `setPreview…Handler` setters. `EditorBuffer` is 58 lines shorter, which restores room under the 10,000-line cap. Internal-only — no behavior, dependency, or `module-info` change.
- **jdtls is pinned to 1.63.0** (from 1.62.0), checked against the jdtls probes. Doctor now names the installed
  jdtls version and warns when it is older than the pinned one, and Install replaces an older copy of Editora's
  own instead of saying it is already installed. Installs made before a pin bump used to keep their server for
  good.
- **Java files up to 50,000 lines keep the language server** in the large-file tier, as Python files do. jdtls
  checks a 12,000-line file in well under a second; above 10,000 lines Java files lost diagnostics, completion
  and navigation.
- **One Java server per Maven reactor or Gradle build outside a project.** Opening files of two modules of one
  reactor in a window without a project started a jdtls per module (1.4 GB each) that could not see the other
  module; the root is now the reactor's or the Gradle build's. A second window on a project another window
  already serves says that it starts a server of its own.
- **Simple mode shows the language-server loading bar,** so a server importing a project in the background is
  visible.
- **Fold All leaves a Java, Kotlin, Scala, Groovy or C# file's one top-level type open** and folds its members,
  imports and comments, the outline IntelliJ's Collapse All gives; before, the file folded to a single line.
- **Type Hierarchy on an interface opens on its subtypes,** the implementations, instead of an empty Supertypes view.
- **The References window shows code for files without a tab,** read in the background, names each file's folder so
  two `Main.java` can be told apart, and says what was searched ("5 references to area in 4 files"). It no
  longer lists the declaration itself.
- **Completion, quick-fix, hover and signature popups open above the caret line** when there is no room below it,
  instead of being pushed up over the line being typed.
- **Static methods and nested types are italic in their own colour,** as in IntelliJ; before, a language server's
  `static` modifier gave them the constant colour, so `String.format` read like a field.
- **Java: Generate hashCode() and equals() starts with every field ticked**, and Enter with nothing ticked in a
  Generate list says so instead of closing silently. The list's rows are taller and it shows twelve at a time.
- **Java: Move lists the test source folders' packages after the main ones,** so a main class is not moved into
  `src/test` by picking the first of two identical package names.
- **Peek Definition works in library source and peeks it.** From a JDK or dependency tab, and on a definition
  inside one, the peek window shows the library source, on the declaration, instead of opening a tab.
- **A member called more than once is one row in Call Hierarchy,** with the count ("append(String) ×2").
- **The References window marks the references that write** — an assignment, `+=`, `++` — with "(write)".
- **Refactor: the text model the editor shares with other packages moved to a new `com.editora.text`.** The LSP value types (`LspTextEdit`, `LspDiagnostic`, `SemanticToken`, `OccurrenceSpan`), `FoldRegions`, the search matcher with `CaseFold` and `SearchMatches`, all of language detection (`LanguageRegistry`, `LanguageNames`, `ConfigFileType`, `ShellFiles`, `ShellScripts`, `Shebang`, `Modeline`) and `EncryptedNames` leave the editor sub-packages, with 13 tests. `lsp`, `search`, `crypto`, `template` and `editops` no longer depend on the editor; `editor.language` is gone, its classes having no presentation in them. `text` has its own 0.95 coverage floor. Internal-only — no behavior, dependency, or `module-info` change.
- **Refactor: the editor's toolkit-free helpers moved to the core packages they belong to.** `AceLabels`,
  `LineEndings`, `RegexLiterals`, `TextNav`, `TextFingerprint` and `WholeDocumentEdit` go to `com.editora.editops`;
  `CompactSource` to `com.editora.run`, `CodeLessLines` to `com.editora.dap`, `PomFiles` to `com.editora.maven` and
  `RulerColumns` to `com.editora.config`, each with its test. `com.editora.index` no longer depends on the editor at
  all. `PomFiles.snippetLanguage(buffer, language)` became `EditorBuffer.snippetLanguage(language)`, so `maven` does
  not reference the editor either. The classes that are the buffer's own state or reference the editor stay:
  `SavedBaseline`, `DocumentSnapshots`, `WordWrap`, `LineMarks`, `TabSurface`, `RunScan`, and `CodeLensShift`, which
  works on RichTextFX types. Internal-only — no behavior, dependency, or `module-info` change.

### Fixed

- **The Default JDK is recognised when it is reached through a symlink.** jdtls's default runtime and the Java it
  runs on compared the Default JDK's resolved path with each JDK's path as found, so a JDK listed through a link (or
  macOS's `/var` → `/private/var`, a Windows short name) lost its place as the default.
- **Markdown: with scroll sync off, the preview no longer jumps once.** A follow queued while sync was on still ran
  after it was switched off; it now checks again. A mode switch still hands the position over.
- **A crash's log is no longer erased by the launch after it.** Each start truncated `editora-session.log`, so the
  log that recorded a crash was gone by the time Editora was reopened to report it. The previous session's file is
  now kept as `editora-session.prev.log` (left out of config exports, like the session log).
- **Java: a jdtls Update no longer leaves other windows without a server.** Doctor's Update stopped jdtls in every
  window but started it again only in the one that ran it. Every window now says the server is paused while it is
  updated, and reopens its Java files when it is done (failed or not); none of them restarts the old server
  meanwhile.
- **Java: Restart restarts only this project's jdtls.** With two projects on one server each, Restart stopped both
  and cleared both projects' problems. Reload Project Configuration now ends on "Loaded and ready", status lines
  name a folder only while two servers run (starting ones included), and a failed import's reason is named by its
  folder too. Reload or Clean in one project keeps another project's failed import and Problems entries, so fixing
  that one's build file still imports it again; a second window on a project that did not import says so and lists
  the project's own problems; a failed import is one error, in the project's own words; one that joins while jdtls
  is still importing waits for it to be ready, rather than
  saying "Loaded and ready" over files not yet checked; and a fix saved in one window clears the old build error in
  the others.
- **Java: jdtls starts when `JAVA_HOME` is a JDK 21.** jdtls 1.63 needs Java 25 though its launcher checks for 21,
  so it crash-looped; Editora reads what the installed jdtls needs at every start (an Update in place included) and
  runs it on a newer JDK it found. With none, the status says "jdtls needs Java 25…", and it stays said (logged
  once).
- **Java: the import chooser waits for you.** Organize Imports and Add all missing imports gave up after 30 s while
  the chooser was still open, and the answer imported nothing; no request times out while it asks, and it closes
  when the server ends (a restart). A second Organize Imports while it asks says to answer it first, a save runs
  none of its on-save actions (clean-up, organize, format) under it, and an answer the file has changed under says so instead of "the server gave up".
- **Java: an open file sees an API changed in another.** Rename a method in one file and save: another open file
  that calls it showed no error, its counter included, until it was typed in. A Java save now rechecks the project
  quietly when another of its files is open, in this window or another sharing its jdtls, as it did only while
  Problems showed the whole project. Outside a Maven project the open files are rechecked without a build, which
  would compile a Gradle project into `bin/`.
- **A tab chosen by its header or by Window ▸ Next Tab has the keyboard focus in its editor**, and so has the tab
  shown when the focused one is closed or split off, or after a right- or middle-click on a header. It stayed on the
  tab pane, the breadcrumbs or the toolbar's New button, so the first keys went nowhere, the arrows switched tabs and
  a Space opened a new buffer.
- **Command palette: one word leads only as a whole title.** "rename" and "find" in a Java file chose the
  terminal's Rename Tab and Find over Rename Symbol and Find in Files, while "project" and "terminal" still open
  their tool windows. The terminal's own commands are grayed while no terminal is open.
- **A jump into a file already open says nothing**, rather than "Already open: Shapes.java".
- **Java: navigation from a library source tab opens library targets.** Go to Super Method, Go to Type Definition
  and a row picked among implementations did nothing from a `jdt://` tab when the target was another library class.
- **Fold All, Unfold All and the other fold-everything commands keep the caret** on its line, or on the fold that
  hides it, and on screen. Each region folded moved it to that region's header, so it ended in another method, off screen.
- **Search Everywhere lists library classes as Go to Symbol does**: `Map.Entry` among the first rows for "Entry",
  not 16th, past the group.
- **Go to Implementation names a nested library class by its own name** (`AbstractList.SubList`), not its outer
  class's.
- **Java: Reload after a failed Gradle import works from `build.gradle`.** Run from the build file's tab, which the
  failure message points to, it updated a project that did not exist. Saving the fixed build file now imports the
  project again too.
- **Java: refactorings keep jdtls in step.** A refactoring that edits a tab jdtls never opened opens it there, so a
  second refactoring before a save no longer skips it. A drag-move of several files is one refactoring: Undo Move
  and Undo Last Refactoring each take all of it back, every file's edit included (also when a file the move edits
  is open in a tab), and either ends the other; the status says what moved and what was kept, not the save's "Saved"
  line, and a move whose edit failed as a failure ("Nothing moved; 1 not moved…"), without covering the warning
  that a package line was left as it was. A drag jdtls edits nothing for, such as a text file, is no
  refactoring, so it leaves the last one (and its own Undo Move) undoable. One drag at a time: a drop while one is
  under way is refused with a message; drop again when it is done (an Undo Move then says to undo it when it is
  done). A folder with no Java in it is not asked about. A Java package named `build`, `out` or `target` moves with its classes. jdtls is told about the destination folder first, a `.java` move it has no package edit
  for says so (not when the destination is the same package, as from main to test), and while it is still loading
  Editora asks once per drag before moving Java files plainly, naming them all. Folders an undo removes are reported
  to it, and a moved folder is checked for Java files off the UI thread.
- **Java: no completion list after a rename or inline**, or after undoing one. An applied edit opened the list at
  the caret, and the next Enter took its first row.
- **Java: Smart Type** binds a type variable by the method's return type (`names.toArray(` into a `String[]` wants a
  `String[]`, not `String[][]`), leaves it open inside another call's argument, and reads the parameter of every
  overload (`System.out.println(` offers an `int`) at the argument the caret is in, also when no overload fits the
  arguments before it; a type variable inside a parameter type is named (`Collection<? extends String>`); a bracket
  inside a string, a char or a comment no longer hides the call.
- **Java: a JDK with its sources is preferred.** Of two JDKs of one version jdtls gets the one with `src.zip`, even
  when the other is the Default JDK or `JAVA_HOME`. A JDK with no sources at all (a distro JDK whose `src.zip` links
  to an uninstalled package, such as Debian's without `openjdk-21-source`) still gives JDK parameters as `arg0`.
- **Java: formatter profiles.** The content-addressed copies are kept in a private folder of this process, checked
  before use and removed when replaced, instead of a shared temporary folder; a server in a container or WSL gets
  the project's own profile; removing a profile (in this session or while Editora was closed), or editing one in
  `.settings` or `config` outside Editora, applies without a restart, in a project window as in one without a
  project, also when the folder comes with it (a checkout). The project's code style now does follow `.editorconfig` and formatter-profile changes without one.
  jdtls still writes its compiler settings into a `.settings` folder the project already has (an Eclipse project's
  committed `org.eclipse.jdt.core.prefs`); a project without one gets none.
- **Java: Add all missing imports asks** which class an ambiguous name means, as Organize Imports does.
- **Complete Statement** reads indentation: a line at the statement's own indent is the next statement, a further
  indented `this.x` goes on. A block that ends a declaration or a `return` closes with `};`, one in an `if (…(x -> {` condition
  with `})) {`, and an annotation leaves the caret at its own indent.
- **Two Java projects in one window** each get their own status line, named by folder, so one's failed import is no
  longer followed by the other's "Loaded and ready". A Maven project's missing dependency is said once, at ready,
  and a fixed `pom.xml` ends on ready.
- Menu rows keep their prefix when two would otherwise read the same ("Rerun Last" twice in Run, "Find in Files" in
  Find and Window). Go to Class puts `Map.Entry` first for "Entry", ranking shaded copies as nested types.
  Implementation rows are sorted by class and line. Refactor This puts what acts on the selection before Extract
  Interface. Postfix completion rows match past the shared qualifier, and the camel-hump matcher no longer slows
  down on long many-word texts. Settings no longer logs an error after an install when its Mermaid page was never
  opened.
- **Java: a failed import names the real cause** (a Gradle build's "Could not find method …", not the generic
  "Could not fetch model"), and belongs to its own project: in a window of several projects one failed import no
  longer marks the others, and it clears once that project imports.
- **Doctor's Update no longer half-deletes an install that is in use.** When another window or program still holds
  the old jdtls open (on Windows), the update is refused with a reason and the old copy stays whole.
- **Java: dragging a `.java` file or package in the Project tree moves the class**: its package line and the
  imports of its users are updated, and Undo Move takes both back. It used to move the file only, and the project
  stopped compiling.
- **Java: a file open in a tab the server has not opened yet** (restored from the last session, or open across a
  restart) is announced when you save it, so the next rename finds it.
- **Java: after a failed Gradle import, Reload Project Configuration imports again.** It restarts the server
  instead of updating a project that does not exist. A Maven project with an unresolved dependency is "loaded, but
  the build has problems", not "did not import"; Clean Java Workspace forgets the failure; run from a `pom.xml` or
  `build.gradle` tab it starts the server again; and the reason no longer carries a stray " PM".
- **Java: "Initialize the field in" shows its choices translated**, not as message keys.
- **Java: Inline Method is chosen from its list**, not run by Ctrl+Alt+N alone, and an action the server cannot
  apply says so.
- **Java: a loose `package demo;` file is rooted where its package says** as it opens, not only after its text has
  loaded: no wrong-package errors and no extra server per package folder.
- **Java: Smart Type completion fills a generic parameter** (`List.of(`, `Optional.of(`, `requireNonNull(`) from
  the declaration's type instead of offering only `null`.
- **Java: Go to Symbol ranks `Map.Entry` sensibly**: nested library types sit below an exact top-level match, not
  below everything, and "Map.Entry" finds it first.
- **Java: the implementation picker names each row's line**, and leaves out the excluded types.
- **Surround With is titled for what it does**, Esc gives back the caret and selection, and a selection over
  several lines wraps the lines it touches.
- **Complete Statement** closes a call around a lambda block (`});`) and leaves a half-typed line where it is.
- **Doctor's Update stops the server in every window** while it replaces the install.
- **Smaller fixes:** the rename and move preview fits its rows; the import chooser asks its question in its title;
  Problems groups project problems under "Project"; the Hierarchy window's count; status lines after a tree rename
  and a Move; plurals in "the rename left 1 new error"; Portuguese terms.
- **Java: refactorings no longer leave the language server behind.** A file a rename or move wrote without a tab
  is announced to jdtls, so the next rename finds it; a file it creates is announced too.
- **Java: renaming or moving a file in the Project tree saves and undoes as one refactoring.** The class is renamed
  with its file, the files jdtls changed are saved, and Undo Last Refactoring moves it back.
- **Java: Move ▸ New package… creates the folder in the project**, not at jdtls's workspace path, and only main
  source roots are offered for main code.
- **Java: Complete Statement leaves a wrapped statement whole** (a stream chain, a ternary, arguments over several
  lines) and closes a new block when the next `}` belongs to the enclosing one.
- **Java: Smart Type completion** finds the type behind a qualifier (`String s = user.`), in a ternary branch and
  at a varargs argument.
- **Java: the project's code style follows `.editorconfig` and formatter-profile changes** without a restart (an
  edited profile is sent under a new name, which is what makes jdtls read it again), and the quiet
  import chooser answers only for the document it was raised for. jdtls's bundle reload no longer logs an error
  on every start.
- **Java: Clean Java Workspace wins against another window's restart**, and a window joining a ready shared server
  says it is ready.
- **Java: a failed import says why** (jdtls's logged reason, not a raw "(WARNING)") and is not then called "Loaded
  and ready"; project-level problems (in `pom.xml` or a Gradle build file) reach Problems when it lists only open
  files; a plain-folder file is no longer red until reopened; the post-import build runs for Maven projects only.
- **Settings ▸ LSP no longer calls an outdated jdtls "Installed".** Its pill says it is older than the release
  Editora is tested with, with Install… to update Editora's copy, as Doctor's Update… does.
- **Java navigation:** a library class opened from Go to Symbol lands on its declaration, not its package line;
  Structure no longer shows a method's return type twice; implementation, type definition and declaration report
  a failed request instead of "nothing found"; a refused rename or code action says the server's reason.
- **Rename and move previews** are as wide as their rows, show project-relative paths and where a moved file goes,
  and say Enter applies.
- **Java editing:** `/**` + Enter lines the closing `*/` up; one Undo reverts everything the actions on save did;
  lambda type hints keep their space (`String s ->`); completion matches a method on its name, not its parameter
  list; signature help shows the active parameter's own description; "Initialize the field in" shows translated
  choices; a second file opened while jdtls starts no longer says "Starting…" again.
- **Java: a folder of `.java` files with packages but no build file is no longer red everywhere.** jdtls guessed
  each file's own folder as its source folder, so `src/demo/Main.java` declaring `package demo` was flagged as
  being in the wrong package and nothing in it resolved. Editora now tells jdtls the source folder the package
  declaration implies as soon as the file is open, the correction Debug already made at launch.
- **Java: whole-project Problems drops errors that were fixed.** With Problems showing the whole project, saving
  a Java file now runs a quiet incremental build, so errors in files that are not open clear once their cause is
  fixed, instead of staying until Build Project was run again.
- **The quick-fix list puts the fix first.** It listed jdtls's actions in the server's order, so "Extract
  interface..." was preselected and the fix for the squiggle sat below ten generators. Fixes now come first, then
  assists, refactorings and source actions; repeated titles are dropped, rows say "Fix", "Refactor" or "Generate"
  instead of LSP kind ids, and for Java the generators moved to Generate. Typing filters the list instead of
  editing the code behind it, and the fixes for a line's problem are offered from anywhere on that line, not
  only with the caret on the squiggle.
- **Java: a refactoring that moves or creates files leaves the disk consistent.** A class rename, Move or
  Extract Interface changed files on disk but left their new text unsaved, so the project did not compile until
  every tab was saved. Every file such a refactoring touches is now saved. A file the refactoring opened only to
  change it is saved and its tab closed, instead of a dirty tab per file.
- **Java: a rename that clashes with an existing name is reported.** jdtls applies it anyway; Editora now checks
  the renamed files afterwards and says how many new errors it left and how to undo it.
- **Java: a pom.xml or build.gradle change reaches the classpath.** jdtls asked "A build file was modified. Do you
  want to synchronize the Java classpath/configuration?" in the status line, where it could not be answered, so a
  dependency added to the pom stayed unresolved. Build files now sync on save (`updateBuildConfiguration:
  automatic`), and jdtls's other questions come with buttons that run its answer.
- **Java: Organize Imports works when a name is ambiguous.** With one `Date` or `List` that could be two classes it
  did nothing and said "Imports already organized". It now asks which class each such name means, and imports the
  rest either way.
- **Java: paste with imports only imports what the pasted code uses.** jdtls resolved every missing import of the
  file, so pasting `int z = 1;` could add an unrelated `import java.time.LocalDate;`.
- **Java: Reload Project Configuration and Build Project work from the pom.xml tab,** where they reached the pom
  language server instead of jdtls. Build Project now says when the build found errors ("Project built with
  errors: see Problems") instead of "Project built".
- **Java: opening a project no longer writes Eclipse files into it.** jdtls put `.project`, `.classpath` and
  `.settings/` into every imported project and module, where they showed up in `git status`. They now stay in
  jdtls's own workspace (`-Djava.import.generatesMetadataFilesAtProjectRoot=false`, as vscode-java does). Files
  written by earlier versions are not removed.
- **Java: Gradle projects import when a newer JDK is installed.** The newest JDK on the machine became jdtls's
  default runtime, and Gradle ran on it; with JDK 27 installed every Gradle 9 import failed while the status bar
  read "1100% Starting Java Language Server". The default is now Settings ▸ Build Tools ▸ Default JDK, else
  `JAVA_HOME`, else the newest, and Gradle is told to run on it.
- **Java: jdtls starts when `JAVA_HOME` points at a JDK older than 21.** Editora now hands jdtls's launcher a JDK
  21 or newer that it finds (the Default JDK when it qualifies), and when there is none it says so instead of
  reporting that the server "keeps crashing".
- **Java: jdtls's memory is capped.** It started with `-Xms1G` and no limit, 1.3–2.5 GB for a small project; it now
  gets vscode-java's defaults (`-Xmx2G`, parallel GC, a small initial heap). A `-Xmx` or GC flag of your own on
  the command or in `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS` still wins.
- **Java: Gradle projects reach "Loaded and ready", and the import narration makes sense.** A Gradle import kept
  sending "Starting" lines after jdtls said it was ready, which kept the ready line from ever coming.
  Percentages past 100 ("1100% Starting Java Language Server") are dropped, and a failed import ("WARNING") is
  reported as an error that says where to look. Opening another file into a server that is already running no
  longer says "Starting Java language server…".
- **Java: the completion documentation popup shows Javadoc.** jdtls computes an item's Javadoc in
  `completionItem/resolve` only when the client lists `documentation` among the properties it resolves; Editora
  listed only `additionalTextEdits`, so the popup showed the return type and nothing else.
- **Java: signature help shows the method's Javadoc.** The setting was sent as `java.signatureHelp.description`;
  jdtls reads `java.signatureHelp.description.enabled`.
- **Java: completion and import quick fixes no longer offer JDK internals** (`sun.*`, `com.sun.*`, `jdk.*`) or
  `java.awt.*`. jdtls installs its type filter only when the client sends one; Editora now sends vscode-java's list,
  editable as Excluded types.
- **Java: inlay hints follow the "all arguments" mode and show inferred types.** jdtls filtered parameter-name
  hints to literals on its own, so the "all" mode changed nothing; it now sends every name and Editora's filter
  applies the mode. `var` declarations and lambda parameters get their inferred type, hints for numbered names
  such as `List.of(e1:, e2:)` are dropped, and an unkinded hint without a trailing `:` or `=` (jdtls's lambda
  parameter type) counts as a type hint, which the literals mode never removes.
- **Java: quick fixes and generated members follow the file's indentation.** jdtls asks the client for
  `java.format.tabSize` and `insertSpaces` before every code action and got no answer, so Generate toString,
  Create method and the other generators indented with tabs in space-indented files.
- **Jumps no longer flicker, and their target is never hidden under the sticky-scroll rows.** A click in the
  Structure panel, Go to Line, a jump to a line from a bookmark, TODO or the Problems list, Go to Definition, a
  search hit and the fold motions all repainted the editor over two or three frames: the caret moved before the
  view, the view jumped before the pinned scope headers changed, and the minimap's viewport box followed a frame
  behind. Each now lands in one frame, and the minimap's box keeps up with every scroll. In the Structure panel
  the row clicked and the row left no longer flash unstyled black text. Go to Line and the fold motions put a
  line above the view below the pinned headers instead of under them, a line already in view is not scrolled
  to, and a jump to the line just inside a method no longer lands under that method's own header.
- **Java: Go to Definition into library source lands on the declaration,** shown below the sticky header, rather
  than on the first line of its Javadoc, under the header; the status bar no longer stays on "Loading library source…" or reads "Editable"
  for the read-only tab.
- **Java: Find References says when it failed or timed out** ("the language server may still be indexing") instead
  of "No references found".
- **Java: completion matches the name, not the parameters.** Without a filter text from the server, `items.st`
  offered `addAll(Collection<? extends Item> c)` and `equals(Object o)` because the parameter list was matched.
- **Opening Problems keeps the caret line in view.** A bottom tool window opening scrolled the line being edited off
  the screen.
- **Problems no longer shows jdtls's numeric problem ids** (`[67108964]`), which linked nowhere.
- **New Java files in Gradle source sets get the right package.** In `src/integrationTest/java` or
  `src/testFixtures/java` the source-set folders became part of the package name.
- **Java: a project's JDK and compliance problems appear after it is imported.** jdtls reports them on the project
  folder, and only a build produced them: a project expecting Java 8 on a machine without one showed odd errors
  and no reason until Build Project. One quiet build now follows each Maven or Gradle import, and such a problem is
  said in the status line and listed in Problems in either scope.
- **The Run Configurations window reopens from the Run dropdown and fits its form.** Picking Edit
  Configurations… a second time did nothing when there were no configurations yet (the dropdown's list stayed on
  that row). The window now opens large enough for its form at a bigger desktop text scale, up to 90% of the
  screen, and the form scrolls above a pinned Save / Close row when the window is shorter.
